newsitem.title: USA: Lone Star Steakhouse grilled after warning.
newsitem.headline: Lone Star Steakhouse grilled after warning.

text.p: Shares in Lone Star Steakhouse & Saloon Inc tumbled 20 percent in heavy trading on Tuesday after the company said its third quarter profits would not meet analysts' expectations.
Jeffries and Co downgraded its rating on the stock to hold from buy citing "deteriorating sales trends and the dramatic earnings shortfall anticipated for the quarter and year."
After the market's close Monday, Lone Star said it expects its third quarter earnings to be $0.10 to $0.13 a share below analysts' forecasts.
Its shares were down 4-7/16 to 17-9/16 in late morning.
According to First Call, 10 analysts were estimating Lone Star's third quarter earnings in a range of $0.45 to $0.50 a share with a mean estimate of $0.47.

Lone Star cited reduced margins due to a "continued decline in average unit volumes" in the first part of the current quarter and planned spending on advertising and marketing in the last half of the year.

"The casual dining environment is likely to remain extremely competitive for some time, without any near-term relief in sight," Jefferies analysts David Rose and James Pott said in a report. "As a consequence, Lone Star will likely see same store sales pressure continuing into the first quarter."
